module_title: Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards History - Foundational Facts
introduction: The highest civilian awards of India are central to the 'Awards and Honors' section of Static GK. Instituted in 1954, the Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards recognize exceptional service and achievements. This foundational level covers the basic hierarchy, original rules, and the first historic recipients.

core_concepts.title: Establishment and Hierarchy
core_concepts.description: The Government of India instituted two civilian awards on January 2, 1954: the Bharat Ratna and the Padma Vibhushan. The official order of precedence is: 1. Bharat Ratna (Highest), 2. Padma Vibhushan, 3. Padma Bhushan, and 4. Padma Shri.

core_concepts.title: Bharat Ratna
core_concepts.description: India's highest civilian honor, awarded for exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor. Traditionally, the number of annual awards is restricted to a maximum of three.

core_concepts.title: The First Laureates (1954)
core_concepts.description: In 1954, the Bharat Ratna was awarded to three monumental figures: C. Rajagopalachari (last Governor-General of India), Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (first Vice-President of India), and Dr. C. V. Raman (Nobel Laureate in Physics).

core_concepts.title: Categories of Padma Awards
core_concepts.description: Padma Awards are divided into three categories: 'Padma Vibhushan' (for exceptional and distinguished service), 'Padma Bhushan' (distinguished service of higher order), and 'Padma Shri' (distinguished service in any field).

important_entities.name: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
important_entities.significance: A great philosopher and statesman whose birthday (September 5) is celebrated as Teachers' Day in India.

important_entities.name: Indira Gandhi
important_entities.significance: The first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna and the first female Prime Minister of India.

important_entities.name: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
important_entities.significance: Also known as 'Frontier Gandhi', he was a Pakistani citizen and a prominent independence activist.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often assume the Bharat Ratna is restricted to Indian citizens. This is a myth. There is no written rule barring foreigners. It has been awarded to two non-Indians: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Pakistan) and Nelson Mandela (South Africa).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the first three recipients, remember the three 'R's from 1954.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct hierarchy questions are frequently asked in tier-1 exams. Always remember the descending order: Ratna > Vibhushan > Bhushan > Shri.
